---
title: "Introduction"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4)
library(parlcat2Rep)
parl_download(quiet = TRUE)
```

*Voices of the Republic* contains the plenary debates of the Parliament of
Catalonia during the Spanish Second Republic, from its constitution in
December 1932 to its last session in October 1938, split into individual
speeches. **parlcat2Rep** loads them into R, with the speaker, their party on
the date of the speech and the office they hold.

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("hunsao/parlcat2Rep")
```

The speech metadata and the reference tables come with the package. The text
of the speeches (about 6 MB) is downloaded once and kept in a cache folder:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(parlcat2Rep)
parl_download()
```

## What is in the corpus

```{r}
meta <- parl_metadata()
meta[c("n_speeches", "n_sessions", "n_words", "n_persons", "period")]
```

There are no sessions in 1935: the Parliament was suspended from October 1934
to February 1936, and it barely met in 1937 and 1938.

```{r}
table(parl_sessions()$any)
```

## Loading speeches

`parl_speeches()` returns one row per speech. Use `text = FALSE` when you only
need the metadata: it is faster and works without the downloaded text.

```{r}
lliga_1934 <- parl_speeches(year = 1934, party = "LR", text = FALSE)
nrow(lliga_1934)
head(lliga_1934[, c("data", "nom_sencer", "party_data", "paraules")])
```

The main filters are `year`, `from` and `to`, `person`, `party`
(`party_data`, the party on the date), `session`, `side` (government or
opposition) and `office`.

```{r}
companys <- parl_speeches(person = "Lluís Companys", include_chair = FALSE)
nrow(companys)
substr(companys$text[1], 1, 200)
```

## Who speaks most

`parl_persons()` gives one row per speaker. The Presidents of the Parliament
lead the raw count because chairing a session produces many short speeches,
so it also gives the counts without chairing.

```{r}
p <- parl_persons()
head(p[order(-p$paraules_sense_presidencia),
       c("nom_sencer", "party", "n_sense_presidencia", "paraules_sense_presidencia")], 8)
```

## Searching the text

```{r}
rab <- parl_search("rabassaires", include_chair = FALSE)
nrow(rab)
table(rab$party_data)

head(parl_kwic("rabassaires", window = 6)[, c("data", "nom_sencer", "pre", "match", "post")], 5)
```

## Trends

`parl_trend()` gives occurrences per million words spoken, so that months with
more debate do not weigh more. The grey band marks the suspension of the
Parliament.

```{r, fig.alt = "Monthly rate of the phrase ordre public per million words, government versus opposition, with the 1934-1936 suspension shaded"}
parl_trend("ordre públic", group = "side", include_chair = FALSE) |>
  parl_plot_trend()
```
